data.name: Sky Sanctuary
data.detailed_description:
Introducing: Taiko Frenzy



If you enjoyed Sky Sanctuary, especially its Taiko mini-game, come and discover Glitchr Studio's new VR rhythm game: Taiko Frenzy. Grab your sticks and play the game now!


Acerca do jogo



Have you ever wanted to be a samurai? Make your dreams come true by joining this mysterious archipelago high in the clouds.

You will follow the instructions of Delios-Sensei, your only friend out there. He will teach you how to progress in the warrior's way and explore the secrets of Zen.

Besides trainings, you will explore all the islands to reveal its secrets. Find inner peace and recharge your batteries contemplating a peaceful environment where nature and technology live in harmony.

Through challenges involving reflection, action, agility and music, prove yourself worthy and eat your way up in leaderboards among the other gakusei.

Welcome to Sky Sanctuary, the mini games collection for true samurais.

Features

  • Master your arsenal: Bow, katana, shaken, smoke bomb, chakram, taiko, flame thrower...
  • Explore the environment: You can move all around the islands and enjoy beautiful panoramas.
  • Make a new friend: Delios, your sensei, will guide you through your journey.
  • Progress at your own pace: Many challenges have several difficulty modes. Whether you are a beginner or a senior samurai, your trainings will fit.
  • Spam the bull's eye: Bend your bow and discover Kyudo (japanese archery). Overcome every challenge on the shooting range and become the real #RobinHoodSama
  • Sharpen your blade: Draw your katana and slice the obstacles in your way with precision and agility. As a Tameshigiri master, look for the perfect moves.
  • Grab your sticks: If you have rhythm in your blood, unleash your skills in the music challenge: will you be a Taiko Hero?
  • Have a break: Enjoy a bit of respite and improve your precision and reflexes in other surprise trials.
  • Move your body: ESky Sanctuary is especially designed for your device and its motion tracking system.
  • Beat the highscores: Compete with your friends all around the world in leaderboards. Become a legend.

General notice

Expect from this game to be physically engaged. You'll have to reproduce real moves from sport activities like archery or martial arts. As you'll have to move your body a lot, especially your arms, make sure that you have a clear playing area (minimum 2m x 1.5m). Stay far enough from your screen and your friends. It would be sad to hurt anyone :).
And like in a real physical activity: don't forget to breathe and take a break! (and drink gallons of water dammit!).

reviews.review:
Sky Sanctuary is a virtual reality action game developed and published by Glitchr Studio that combines martial arts practice, precision-based gameplay, and peaceful exploration within a floating world suspended high above the clouds. Instead of relying on an elaborate storyline or constant combat encounters, the game focuses on personal mastery, encouraging players to refine their techniques through a variety of physical challenges. Guided by a wise master, players gradually learn the disciplines of the samurai while uncovering the secrets hidden throughout the serene sanctuary. Its blend of action and relaxation creates an experience that stands apart from many traditional VR titles, offering both entertainment and a surprisingly calming atmosphere.

The gameplay revolves around movement and accuracy, making full use of virtual reality's immersive controls. Players engage in sword training by slicing bamboo, targets, and other objects with carefully timed swings rather than frantic motions. Every strike rewards precision, encouraging players to develop proper technique instead of simply relying on speed. Archery serves as another major activity, requiring steady aim and careful control to hit distant targets consistently. These mechanics transform each session into a combination of skill development and physical exercise, making every successful challenge feel genuinely earned through practice and improvement.

Beyond its combat-inspired activities, Sky Sanctuary emphasizes exploration across its collection of floating islands. The environment is designed to encourage curiosity, with scenic landscapes, hidden pathways, and small discoveries rewarding those who take the time to look around. A robotic companion accompanies players throughout their journey, adding personality to the otherwise tranquil setting while helping guide exploration. Although exploration remains relatively straightforward, the beautifully crafted surroundings create a peaceful contrast to the demanding training exercises, giving players opportunities to relax between more intense gameplay segments.

Progression is centered on overcoming increasingly difficult trials that test reaction speed, coordination, and consistency. Rather than introducing complex RPG systems or extensive customization, the game focuses on refining player skill through repeated practice. Leaderboards and score-based challenges provide additional motivation for players who enjoy chasing personal bests or competing against others. This replay-oriented structure gives the experience lasting appeal despite its relatively modest amount of content, particularly for players who appreciate mastering mechanics over time rather than simply completing a linear campaign.

Visually, the game succeeds by presenting a colorful and inviting world that complements its themes of balance and discipline. The floating sanctuary, expansive skies, and stylized architecture create a relaxing atmosphere that feels almost meditative. While the graphics are not intended to push cutting-edge realism, the artistic presentation effectively supports the game's focus on serenity and concentration. Combined with responsive motion controls and satisfying weapon interactions, the presentation enhances immersion without distracting from the core gameplay experience.

The game does have a few shortcomings that may limit its appeal to certain audiences. Players searching for a lengthy story, numerous enemy encounters, or extensive progression systems may find the overall package somewhat limited. Most activities revolve around improving performance within existing challenges, which means the experience depends heavily on the player's willingness to replay content and perfect their skills. Some of the physical movements can also become tiring during longer sessions, especially for newcomers to virtual reality who are still adjusting to room-scale gameplay.

Despite these limitations, Sky Sanctuary remains an enjoyable and thoughtfully designed VR experience that successfully delivers on its vision. It combines accessible martial arts mechanics, rewarding skill progression, and peaceful environmental design into a package that values focus and discipline over nonstop action. The result is a game that feels equally suited for players looking for a relaxing escape or those who enjoy honing their reflexes through repeated practice. While it may not offer the scale or depth of larger VR adventures, its polished mechanics and distinctive atmosphere make it a worthwhile addition to any virtual reality library.

Rating: 7/10
